sections.h2: Mason County tax offices in Maysville
sections.html:
All three offices are in Maysville. One sets the value, one collects this year's bill, and the third records deeds and inherits any bill that stays unpaid.

  • PVA: 220 1/2 Sutton Street, (606) 564-3700, staffed through the workweek. It handles value, mailing and property addresses, and exemptions.
  • Sheriff: 120 West Third Street, in the old Health Department building, 606-564-3309, doors open at nine on weekdays, and a drop box takes checks only.
  • Clerk: 27 West 3rd Street, PO Box 234, (606) 564-3341, opening at eight on weekdays and closing for lunch between 11:30 and 12:30.

Before disputing a bill, know what the PVA controls. The office writes no laws and sets no rates, and it does not take payments either, so keep your checkbook for the sheriff. Fiscal court members, city officials and school boards vote the rates, so a rate complaint goes to them.

sections.h2: The Ohio River and the Mason County market
sections.html:
Mason County is a river county in northeastern Kentucky, with the Ohio River along its northern edge, facing Brown and Adams counties in Ohio. Maysville is both seat and largest city. Dover, Germantown and Sardis are the other incorporated places, and Mays Lick is a census-designated place.

Population has eased: 17,490 in 2010, 17,120 in 2020, and an estimate of 16,936, which is 1.1 percent under the 2020 base. The county has 8,276 housing units and 7,131 households, and owners live in 66.1 percent of homes. The median home value is $161,500. Median gross rent is $727, and owners with a mortgage pay a median of $1,245 a month, compared with $405 for owners without one. Only 26 building permits were issued in 2025, so resale homes make up most of what a buyer sees. Expect buyers to compare your house with older river-town homes in Maysville and with houses in the smaller towns, and expect their lenders to ask for the tax bill. Mason County Schools is the single public district.

The sheriff's Taxpayer's Notice sets out four periods, and the bill itself arrives on a yellow postcard.

Mason County payment periods
PeriodAmount owed
October 1 to November 1Face amount minus a two percent discount
Next two monthsFace amount
January onlyFace plus a five percent penalty
February to April 15Face plus a twenty-one percent penalty

The usual timetable is set out in KRS 134.015. After April 15, real estate bills pass to the County Clerk, where a County Attorney fee of 20 percent, a clerk fee of 10 percent and interest of 1 percent monthly are charged, and an investor may buy the delinquency. A prior-year bill is paid at the clerk's counter, and the payoff number is 606-564-3341.

Past-due reminders are never mailed. A bounced check costs $50 and returns the bill to unpaid. Cards work through the online link with a surcharge. If escrow or a new owner is responsible, pass the notice along at once.

Appeals begin at the PVA: talk the value over, review how it was figured, and take it to the Board of Appeals if nothing is resolved. The city of Maysville seats an appointee on that board and lists the PVA, (606) 564-3700, as the contact.

Appraisers see each property at least every four years and may measure a building's outside when nobody is home. In the statute, KRS 133.120 sets the order of steps, and KRS 133.030 puts the board's first meeting 25 to 35 days after inspection closes. Carry evidence of value and keep paying on your claimed figure until the board rules. A paid representative has to come from the professions the statute lists.

Good evidence is concrete. Bring photos of any damage or deferred repairs, recent sale prices of comparable houses nearby, an appraisal if you paid for one, and the property record card the PVA can show you. Compare the square footage, bedroom count and condition on that card with the house you actually own, since a wrong detail is the easiest error to correct. Ask the PVA to note your concerns in writing at the conference so the board sees them.

For 2025 and 2026 the exemption is $49,100 off assessed value. Qualifying owners live in the house and are 65 or older, or totally disabled. Applicants go to the PVA page on the county website, which also hosts a property search and a vehicle-tax exoneration affidavit. An approved age claim normally carries on while the same owner stays in the house; a buyer files afresh.

The sheriff quotes this year's balance and the clerk quotes earlier years, and both come out of the sale proceeds. Under KRS 134.015(5) a delinquency lien can survive eleven years whoever holds title, so title agents insist on payoff.

Deeds are filed with the clerk at 27 West 3rd Street. The seller's transfer tax is fifty cents on each $500 of value under KRS 142.050. For electronic filing the clerk lists Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile and ePN. Confirm what each deed needs before sending it.

Before you sign, use the property search on the county's PVA page to check that the owner name and mailing address on file match what the deed will say, and ask the PVA to correct any mismatch so the next tax bill reaches the right person.

Start with three calls. The sheriff gives you the current balance, the clerk tells you whether any earlier year is open, and the PVA confirms the name, address and exemption on the roll. Ask each for a written figure and the date it stays good, because the sheriff's notice and the clerk's fees move the number as the calendar advances.

Bring the deed, a photo ID and your latest bill, and if the house came to you by inheritance, bring whatever shows your authority to sell. Give the payoff letters to the title agent so each amount is paid from the proceeds at the table. With a cash sale there is no lender waiting on an appraisal, so a clean tax record is the main thing that keeps the closing on its date.

If a bill is missing, call the sheriff for a copy, since reminders are never mailed and a lost postcard does not stop penalties from running. If an escrow account pays your tax, ask the lender to confirm the payment went out before you list, and ask the closing agent to refund any unused escrow balance to you after the sale. Keep your receipts in one folder for the title agent.

faqs.q: What are the Mason County Sheriff's office hours?
faqs.a: The office opens at nine on weekdays, at 120 West Third Street in Maysville. Call 606-564-3309. A drop box takes checks only.

faqs.q: What does a bounced check cost on a Mason County tax bill?
faqs.a: It costs $50. The bill returns to unpaid status, and your repayment should follow the payment period printed on it.

faqs.q: Does the Mason County Sheriff mail past-due notices?
faqs.a: No. None is mailed, so watch the dates. Real estate bills still open after April 15 pass to the County Clerk with added fees.

faqs.q: Who sets tax rates in Mason County?
faqs.a: Elected bodies do: the fiscal court, city officials and school boards, among other taxing authorities. The PVA neither sets rates nor decides the total to be raised.

faqs.q: Can a Mason County bill be paid by card?
faqs.a: Yes, through the online link on the sheriff's site, where the card company adds a charge. Counter payments, mail and the check-only drop box also work.
